name: Russia–NATO
value: Drone in Polish airspace 23 Nov; no Article 4
summary: Russian drone entered Polish airspace 23 Nov; Poland plans border no-fly zone; NATO won't back intercepts over Ukraine
state: Polish forces were cleared to shoot down a Russian drone that entered Polish airspace on the evening of 23 Nov but held fire when it turned back towards Ukraine, the Operational Command said on 24 Nov; three Kh-101 cruise missiles crashed in Poland on 20 Nov (United24). On 25 Nov deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk said Poland plans a no-fly zone along its border by early 2027 and that NATO does not support intercepting Russian missiles over Ukraine (Kyiv Independent). No Article 4 request was found, so Watch holds.
for_you: People near NATO's eastern borders should follow local civil defence guidance. Travellers should check FCDO advice for Poland and the Baltic states.
rubric_hit: Airspace violations by Russian drones and missiles = Watch; no Article 4 or direct clash

sources.title: United24 Media — Russian drone enters NATO airspace; Poland decides not to shoot
Kyiv Independent — Poland plans no-fly zone near Ukraine border, asks NATO to intercept Russian missiles

why: Direct Russia–NATO confrontation is the most likely path to a European war involving the UK.
drivers: Airspace and drone incursions, sabotage, Baltic incidents, nuclear signalling, Ukraine war spillover.

rubric.alert: Article 4 consultations, a direct military clash, or an attack on NATO territory.
rubric.watch: Airspace/drone violations, sabotage attributed to Russia, or explicit threats against members.
rubric.normal: No notable incidents on NATO territory in the past two weeks.
